title: FastAPI Backend Bootstrap
description: Create the HTTP application using FastAPI as the backend entry point and configure the project for API execution.
acceptance: FastAPI is installed and configured as a project dependency.
The application starts successfully using a standard ASGI server.
The API exposes a health endpoint returning HTTP 200.
The project structure separates application, domain, and infrastructure concerns.

title: Mock Market Data Resources
description: Provide realistic market data fixtures for BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT using the MarketData model schema.
acceptance: JSON resources exist for BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT.
Each JSON document conforms to analysis.models.market.MarketData.
Mock resources are stored under a dedicated resources directory.
The mock data can be loaded without code changes.

title: Market Data Provider
description: Define a MarketDataProvider port and adapter implementations that allow the application to retrieve MarketData independently of the underlying data source.
acceptance: A MarketDataProvider port defines the contract for retrieving MarketData.
A MockMarketDataProvider adapter loads MarketData objects from JSON resources.
Application and domain logic depend only on the MarketDataProvider port.
New adapters can be added or substituted without modifying application or domain code.

title: Analysis to Classification Pipeline
description: Connect the deterministic analysis module with the classification module using the existing assessment_to_classifications mapper.
acceptance: MarketData is processed by the deterministic analysis module.
Analysis assessments are transformed using assessment_to_classifications.py.
The classifier module receives only mapped DTOs.
No direct coupling exists between analysis internals and the classifier.

title: Classification REST API
description: Expose classification results through a REST API endpoint using DTOs instead of domain objects.
acceptance: The API accepts a market symbol as input.
The endpoint returns the current classification DTO.
HTTP responses use API DTOs rather than domain models.
Invalid requests return appropriate HTTP status codes.
